title: Cap. VI Arg. 10: Rom. 9 — Jacob and Esau; objection of injustice referred to Rom. 11:33-34
pass_a_gloss: This is shown by the Apostle, Rom. 9, where the gratuitous election of Jacob and the passing by of Esau being declared, he at once removes that objection which human reason suggests, namely, Such a good pleasure being posited, according to which of brothers not yet born, before they had done anything good or evil, one is loved, the other hated, that there is a certain injustice with God, verse 14. Which objection he solves by not solving, while he teaches that it is to be referred to the inscrutable height of Divine wisdom and judgment, Rom. 11:33-34.
pass_b_english: Paul shows it in Rom. 9: after stating Jacob's gratuitous election and Esau's being passed by, he at once thrusts off the objection human reason prompts — that if by such good pleasure one unborn brother is loved and the other hated before either did good or evil, there is injustice with God (v. 14). He solves it by not solving it: he sends it up to the inscrutable height of divine wisdom and judgment (Rom. 11:33-34).
source_text: Ostentum est hoc ab Apostolo, Rom. ix. ubi gratuita Jacobi electione et Esavi praeteritione declarata, statim amolitur illam objectionem, quam humana ratio suggerit, nimirum, Posito tali beneplacito, secundum quod nondum natis fratribus, priusquam nihil fecissent boni vel mali, unus diligatur, alter odio habeatur, injustitiam quandam esse apud Deum, vers. 14. Quam objectionem non solvendo solvit, dum ad inscrutabilem altitudinem sapientiae ac judicii Divini referendam docet, Rom. xi. vers. 33. 34.
